spike_notes: Rank-two ultimate and coordinated mid-game fights
reasoning: Aatrox converts levels, ability haste and sustained access into a strong mid-game fight. His output depends on landing chained abilities and receiving enough resources to survive through healing windows.
Annie offers a direct burst-and-engage plan whose most important windows depend on stun preparation and access to the target rather than a complex mechanical sequence.

spike_notes: Prepared weapon cycle before an objective
reasoning: Aphelios is a resource-intensive carry whose fight output rises with items and deliberate weapon preparation. The composition must create safe space and arrive with the correct setup.
Braum contributes primarily through protection, counter-engage and passive coordination. His value depends more on enemy access patterns and allied follow-up than personal gold.
Caitlyn can create early lane and structure pressure, but the draft must convert that control and bridge item-dependent troughs. Trap setup and protected range determine later fight access.
Ezreal converts early item completions and repeated skill-shot access into mid-game pressure. His safety is valuable, but missed abilities sharply reduce the composition's damage output.

spike_notes: Early levels with access to all basic abilities
reasoning: Lee Sin creates early access, skirmish and displacement windows. The value of the pick depends on converting tempo and executing the correct role as raw damage becomes less central later.

spike_notes: Ultimate available against an exposed carry
reasoning: Vi provides reliable single-target access and a direct engage signal. She is strongest when the composition can immediately follow her commitment and convert the isolated target.
Xerath converts items and prepared space into long-range health advantages. His output is execution-sensitive and drops when opponents bypass the setup phase.
Support Xerath trades lower guaranteed income for early range pressure. The pick must create lane or setup value while avoiding direct engage and flank access.
Zyra creates lane pressure and prepared zone control without requiring carry-level income. Her strongest fights begin in controlled terrain before opponents gain clean access.

spike_notes: Vision-controlled arrow angle before an objective
reasoning: Ashe gives bot lane reliable initiation, chase control and pick access without needing the highest economy share. Her draft value rises when the team can convert Hawkshot information and Enchanted Crystal Arrow into coordinated first moves.

Draven is a lane-pressure and snowball carry whose draft asks for early support, wave access and protection against forced resets. If the team cannot convert his first windows, his resource demand becomes a structural cost.

spike_notes: Two- to three-item pick and objective setup
reasoning: Jhin supports picks and engages from range before converting control into burst damage. He needs prepared spacing and struggles to provide continuous damage into several durable targets without allied setup.

Jinx is a high-resource scaling carry who wants peel, frontline and enough fight duration to trigger resets. Drafts around her should identify how the first takedown is created and how she survives enemy access.

Kalista wants lane agency, support coordination and early objective conversion. Her draft value is strongest when the team can fight on tempo around Rend and Fate's Call rather than waiting for pure late scaling.

Lucian offers short-range burst tempo and lane pressure, especially when paired with enablers that let him enter trades safely. The draft must convert his early-mid pressure before range and scaling disadvantages become expensive.

spike_notes: Layered crowd control into Bullet Time
reasoning: Miss Fortune supplies straightforward area fight damage and punishes locked targets. She is most valuable when the draft can hold opponents in a cone and force fights in corridors or objective setups.

spike_notes: Global ultimate swing in a cross-map fight
reasoning: Bot Senna trades conventional carry tempo for range growth, utility and global influence. She asks the draft to clarify who farms, who fronts the lane, and how the team survives until her range and utility matter.

spike_notes: Grouped fight with allied shielding or engage
reasoning: Nilah is a short-range melee bot carry who needs entry support and durable fight structure. Her payoff is strongest when allied engage, shielding or sustain lets her stay in range long enough to convert clustered fights.

spike_notes: Allied knock-up or hard engage available
reasoning: Samira is a reset-oriented dive carry who needs reliable entry cues and protection while stacking style. She should be drafted with clear engage partners and against comps that cannot easily deny her first commitment.

Bot Seraphine turns wave control, sustain and layered crowd control into grouped fight value. She is strongest when the draft wants five-on-five structure and has another source of reliable sustained damage.

spike_notes: On The Hunt engage or disengage timing
reasoning: Sivir gives wave control, team speed and durable front-to-back damage if she reaches item windows. Drafts around her can neutralize lanes and then force grouped tempo, but she still needs protection and time.

spike_notes: Late grouped fight with safe front line
reasoning: Smolder is a scaling carry whose draft must buy time and protect stacking access. His value rises sharply when the team can avoid forced early collapses and arrive at fights with enough front line to let him cast repeatedly.

spike_notes: Extended fight where enemies cannot disengage
reasoning: Bot Swain changes the lane into a durable magic-damage fight pattern. He wants opponents pulled into extended ranges and benefits from allies who can start fights or keep enemies inside his drain window.

Bot Tristana is an income-dependent carry who converts resets and explosive-charge windows into kills or structures. Her jump can follow a secured target, but using it as unsupported primary engage removes an important safety tool.

spike_notes: Objective setup with poke or Chain of Corruption
reasoning: Varus changes identity by build: poke and siege plans want early setup, while on-hit plans ask for protected sustained damage. The draft must state which Varus it is selecting so the rest of the composition answers the same timing.
Xayah is a scaling anti-dive carry who punishes enemies entering her feather field. She is strongest when the opponent must come forward and her team can buy the space needed for blade recall threat.

Bot Brand provides magic damage, wave control and area punishment from the carry slot. He is strongest when enemies must group into choke points and weaker when the draft needs a traditional protected physical DPS threat.

Bot Corki brings mixed poke and scaling damage with strong objective setup around package windows. His draft needs time, wave access and a plan for surviving until his item and package timings can shape fights.

spike_notes: Plasma access from allied crowd control
reasoning: Kai'Sa is a scaling dive marksman whose best drafts give her plasma setup, isolated target access and enough economy to hit evolutions. The comp must decide whether she is playing front-to-back cleanup or back-line follow-up.

spike_notes: Grouped fight where passive value is unavoidable
reasoning: Bot Karthus supplies heavy magic DPS and global execute pressure from a farming lane. He wants the team to accept lower conventional marksman utility in exchange for scaling damage and unavoidable fight cleanup.

spike_notes: Late fight with peel cooldowns available
reasoning: Kog'Maw is a high-resource hypercarry who pays off when the draft can protect a stationary damage source. His value depends less on starting fights and more on surviving long enough to melt frontline and objectives.

spike_notes: Spray and Pray angle through multiple targets
reasoning: Bot Twitch is an ambush scaling carry who converts unseen angles into fight starts or cleanup. Drafts around him need protection after reveal and enough map control to make stealth pressure credible.

spike_notes: Final Hour fight with space to tumble
reasoning: Bot Vayne is a short-range scaling duelist and tank killer. She needs draft protection, side-space or peel to survive early pressure and convert late fights where her single-target DPS can keep firing.

spike_notes: Event Horizon controlling a choke point
reasoning: Bot Veigar offers scaling magic burst and powerful zone denial from the carry slot. He is strongest when the draft can play around cage control and does not require immediate physical DPS from bot lane.

Zeri is a high-execution scaling kite carry. She needs time, space and fight length; the draft should protect her early economy and avoid forcing short fights before she can stack movement and damage.

spike_notes: Objective setup with minefield and long-range poke
reasoning: Bot Ziggs shifts the lane toward wave control, siege and structure pressure. He helps drafts that want to avoid standard marksman trading and instead win through tempo, poke and tower conversion.

spike_notes: Grouped objective fight with Flash or Bandage Toss access
reasoning: Amumu gives reliable engage, frontline and area lockdown without needing carry-level economy. His draft value rises when the team has follow-up damage for his first commitment and wants simple five-on-five fight structure.
Bel'Veth is a resource-hungry skirmish and objective snowball jungler. She needs lanes that can contest entrances and create first resets so her scaling and objective conversion become real pressure.

spike_notes: Enemy team grouped around a neutral objective
reasoning: Jungle Brand supplies high magic damage, fast area clear and punishing objective fights. His drafts need lanes or supports to provide reliable engage or protection because his own access and escape tools are limited.

Briar is a commitment jungler whose power comes from forced access, dueling and chaotic skirmishes. The draft must control when she enters fights, because poor target selection or disengage-heavy opponents can punish her forced movement.

Jungle Cho'Gath brings frontline, silence disruption and strong objective secure. He wants slower, structured games where his durability and Feast threat matter more than early tempo or repeated ganks.

Jungle Darius is an off-pattern bruiser pick that wants close-range skirmishes and extended fights. He needs lane setup or enemy face-checks because he lacks reliable long-range engage compared with standard junglers.

spike_notes: Multi-target Moonfall setup with allied follow-up
reasoning: Jungle Diana provides AP dive and area engage from the jungle slot. She wants drafts that can layer damage into her ultimate and protect against disengage after her first commitment.

spike_notes: Extended fight where anti-heal is not fully layered
reasoning: Jungle Dr. Mundo gives durable frontline and attrition rather than precise engage. He fits drafts that need a low-execution meat shield, but he asks teammates to provide lockdown and reliable back-line damage.
Jungle Ekko is a scaling AP skirmisher and pick threat who needs setup time and flank access. He can punish isolated targets hard, but drafts should not rely on him as the only guaranteed engage.

Elise is an early-pressure jungler built around dives, picks and tempo conversion. She needs lanes that can move or set up Cocoon, because falling behind without early conversion leaves her draft with less scaling insurance.
Evelynn is a stealth pick jungler who warps enemy positioning after level 6. Her draft needs enough early stability to reach that point and enough objective control to turn picks into map gains.

spike_notes: First AP or utility jungle item
reasoning: Fiddlesticks provides devastating zone engage from fog and strong objective-area threat. He is draft-dependent on vision denial and setup time; without flank darkness, his engage becomes much easier to manage.

spike_notes: Explosive Cask isolating a priority target
reasoning: Jungle Gragas is a flexible engage, disengage and pick tool. His exact curve depends on build, but the draft value is his ability to start fights, split teams or deny enemy access with one high-impact displacement.

spike_notes: Objective fight with smoke screen value
reasoning: Graves is a farming and skirmish jungler who converts tempo, camps and lane priority into damage leads. He offers damage and objective pressure, but drafts still need other champions to supply reliable engage or peel.

spike_notes: Frontline target access without being kited
reasoning: Jungle Gwen is a scaling AP side and objective fighter who wants farm and extended fights. She needs drafts that can buy time and help her enter fights, because she is not a natural early gank or hard engage solution.

Hecarim is a tempo and dive jungler who converts movement speed into back-line access. He needs resources and flank angles, and his best drafts can follow his first fear rather than leaving him isolated.

spike_notes: Carry shield cycle around objective fight
reasoning: Ivern is a supportive jungle enabler who trades personal damage for peel, shields and unusual pathing. He needs a clear carry target and teammates who benefit from extra protection or brush control.

Jarvan IV supplies early tempo, reliable engage and target containment. He is strongest when teammates can damage trapped targets and weakest when opponents can consistently disengage or punish his flag-and-drag commitment.

spike_notes: Side-lane or skirmish window after jungle tempo
reasoning: Jungle Jax is a scaling duelist and dive threat. He needs farm and skirmish access more than pure utility, so drafts should provide lanes that survive early and later let him pressure sides or back-line entries.

Jungle Jayce is an off-pattern physical poke and tempo pick. He demands execution, lane priority and clear draft purpose because he does not naturally cover frontline, peel or reliable engage from the jungle slot.
Jungle Karthus is a farming AP damage engine whose pressure comes from clear speed, global damage and late fight output. The draft must cover early map stability and provide engage or peel elsewhere.

Kayn's jungle identity depends on form: Shadow Assassin leans toward pick and back-line access, while Rhaast gives bruiser sustain and frontline fighting. Drafts should treat form timing as the real first spike.
Kha'Zix is a pick and isolation jungler who wants fog, side pressure and enemy spacing mistakes. The draft should avoid needing him as primary frontline or guaranteed engage.

spike_notes: Protected objective fight with range advantage
reasoning: Kindred is a marksman jungler who brings scaling damage and a fight-reset ultimate. She needs lanes that can contest marks and a draft that can protect or exploit Lamb's Respite instead of being trapped by it.
Lillia is a speed-based AP skirmisher who wants extended spacing and multi-target setup. Her drafts should create room to kite and then collapse when sleep turns poke into engage.
Jungle Malphite is a simple engage and armor-scaling utility pick. His pre-6 agency is limited, so the draft must survive early tempo and be ready to convert his first ultimate window.

spike_notes: Objective setup with saplings and Nature's Grasp
reasoning: Jungle Maokai provides reliable engage, peel and vision-like objective control without demanding high economy. He fits drafts that need structure and follow-up more than personal carry damage.

Master Yi is a reset hypercarry jungler who needs resources, cleanup timing and protection from targeted crowd control. Drafts around him should create the first low-health target and avoid forcing him to start fights.

spike_notes: Objective fight where one enemy must be removed
reasoning: Jungle Mordekaiser offers AP bruiser damage and isolation through Realm of Death. He is strongest when removing one key enemy breaks the opponent's fight plan or objective contest.

Jungle Morgana gives magic clear speed, binding pick threat and anti-CC utility. Her drafts benefit from teammates that can capitalize on Dark Binding and from opponents whose engage is softened by Black Shield.

spike_notes: Isolated carry access after poke or vision denial
reasoning: Jungle Naafiri is a direct physical pick and dive threat. She wants clear target access and allied damage to finish her commitment before peel and grouped formations shut down her angle.

spike_notes: First durability item with Wither target access
reasoning: Jungle Nasus is a scaling utility bruiser with Wither and objective threat, but low early pressure. His draft must buy time and provide map agency elsewhere while he stacks toward a durable mid-late role.

Nidalee is an execution-heavy tempo jungler built around invade pressure, poke and fast conversion. She needs lane priority and accurate spear setup because she offers limited fallback engage or frontline.

spike_notes: Ultimate available against an isolated carry
reasoning: Nocturne turns darkness and long-range access into a clear single-target commitment. He needs lanes or allied control to finish the target and becomes vulnerable when entering the full enemy protection layer alone.
Nunu & Willump is a tempo, gank and objective-control jungler. The pick wants lanes that can follow early snowballs and a draft that values secure and map tempo over personal carry damage.
Jungle Olaf is an early skirmish and anti-CC run-down threat. He needs tempo and target access; if the enemy can kite without relying on crowd control, his engage pattern becomes easier to exhaust.
Jungle Pantheon is an early pick and map-tempo tool. He wants lanes that can convert his stun and a draft that snowballs before his raw scaling becomes less central.

spike_notes: Steadfast Presence denying enemy dash engage
reasoning: Jungle Poppy is an anti-dive and displacement tank who punishes dash-heavy opponents. She is strongest as a counter-structure pick when the enemy composition must enter through mobility.
Jungle Qiyana is a high-execution AD pick and terrain-fight champion. She needs flank access, terrain awareness and enough early tempo to avoid being outscaled before her burst windows matter.
Rammus is a counter-pick tank into physical attackers and auto-attack carries. He brings fast engage and lockdown, but his value drops when opponents are magic-heavy or can kite his first roll.

Alistar supplies reliable short-range engage or counter-engage without requiring income. His draft value depends on choosing between starting the fight and holding cooldowns to protect allied damage dealers.

Camille converts solo-lane income into side-lane pressure and reliable target isolation. In team fights she needs a synchronized entry or follow-up because committing beyond the frontline can separate her from allied damage.

spike_notes: A marked target separated from protection
reasoning: Locke is a setup-dependent assassin whose teleporting pursuit and missing-health damage reward decisive target selection. He needs income and a prepared entry, while failed commitment spends health and position without guaranteeing an exit.

Nautilus provides layered single-target control and can either force a carry or peel a diver. He does not need much income, but missed or poorly chosen engage angles can leave him isolated from allied follow-up.

Renekton converts early lane resources, fury and flank access into durable mid-game pressure. His threat drops when opponents deny early conversion or force him to enter without fury and allied follow-up.

spike_notes: First completed fighter or tank item
reasoning: Trundle offers direct skirmish strength, objective damage and terrain disruption. He is most valuable into durable frontliners and short-range fights, while mobile or ranged opponents can deny sustained attack access.

spike_notes: First ability upgrade and mana completion
Prepared choke point around an objective
reasoning: Viktor converts lane income and completed upgrades into wave control and sustained area damage. He needs space and time for repeated spell rotations; direct multi-angle access can prevent him from establishing the fight zone.

spike_notes: Death Sentence, Dark Passage and Flay are all available
Level 6 with The Box available for a committed fight
Dark Passage ready before an ally enters danger
reasoning: Thresh can start a catch or hold tools to interrupt entry and move an ally to safety. The value of either route depends on landing the control, keeping the lantern available and having allied follow-up; a missed hook alone does not establish a lost fight.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Thresh abilities

spike_notes: Level 6 with Call of the Forge God available
Masterwork item upgrades become available to the team
Allied follow-up is in range before the second ultimate cast
reasoning: Ornn combines frontline access and area control with later item-upgrade value. His ultimate needs a viable approach and allied damage in range; the upgrade economy does not by itself establish winning lane priority or a favorable early skirmish.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Ornn abilities

spike_notes: Whimsy and Help, Pix! ready as enemy access begins
An allied damage dealer is positioned to use the protection
reasoning: Lulu's support value depends on choosing when to use her spells for allied protection or offensive pressure. She can strengthen a carry and disrupt an entry, but the team needs a protected damage source and cannot assume both uses of the same cooldown at once.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Lulu abilities

spike_notes: A first takedown creates a Sovereign's Domination possession window
Allied control and damage can secure the first reset target
reasoning: Viego's fight route becomes more threatening after the first takedown because possession gives him another set of basic abilities and a free ultimate cast. Before that reset, access, target selection and allied setup matter; the draft should not count later possessions as guaranteed power.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Viego abilities

spike_notes: Living Shadow ready for entry or exit
Energy and a safe shadow route are available before committing
reasoning: Zed threatens an exposed target through shadow access and a committed burst window. Shadow placement and energy determine whether he can leave safely; enemy protection and grouped positioning can deny the intended target even when his ultimate is ready.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Zed abilities

spike_notes: Transcendent ability upgrades earned through Splinters of Wrath
Scatter the Weak ready before committing to a pick
reasoning: Syndra can threaten a target with sphere setup and a burst window while holding Scatter the Weak to interrupt an approach. Her upgraded abilities depend on earned Splinters of Wrath; an early draft must not assume those upgrades or a safe firing position are already present.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Syndra abilities

spike_notes: Tidecaller's Blessing ready when an ally can reach a target
Aqua Prison available to follow up or stop an approach
reasoning: Nami can support a trade with ally movement, added damage and healing, then use her control for a catch or counter-engage. Her offensive value needs an ally who can make contact; committing Aqua Prison early leaves less control for the next enemy entry.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Nami abilities

spike_notes: Courage ready before taking a committed trade
Time outside enemy damage to use Perseverance
reasoning: Garen can threaten a close-range target after reaching them and can recover health between trades when enemy pressure lets his passive run. Courage helps him survive a commitment, but limited access to distant targets and repeated damage that interrupts recovery can deny this route.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Garen abilities

spike_notes: Level 6 with Breath of Life available
Cozy Campfire and Warm Hugs ready for an allied carry
Breath of Life held until an enemy control commitment
reasoning: Milio increases the space and safety available to an allied damage dealer, and his ultimate can answer a committed control sequence. This depends on an ally positioned to use the range and protection; a forced ultimate or an enemy reaching Milio first reduces the value of the defensive window.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Milio abilities

Critical-strike items support Vow of the First Lands
A protected attack route is available before entering Transcendent State
reasoning: Yunara's critical strikes add magic damage and her ultimate opens a stronger temporary ability window. She still needs gold, repeated attack access and protection to deliver that damage; the temporary state does not guarantee a safe route through enemy engage.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Yunara abilities

spike_notes: Basic abilities available for a terrain-assisted approach
A target can be reached for the third Wound stack and follow-up attack
reasoning: Jungle Talon can use terrain routes to approach an exposed target, then convert stacked Wounds into burst. He needs a reachable target and a route out after committing; mobility alone does not supply frontline or a guaranteed first takedown.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Talon abilities

spike_notes: Mantra and Inner Flame ready for lane pressure
Mantra and Inspire ready before allied repositioning
Focused Resolve can remain connected to the chosen target
reasoning: Support Karma can spend Mantra on damage and space or reserve it for allied protection and movement. The team cannot count both empowered uses from one Mantra cast; the value of her control also depends on maintaining contact rather than merely starting a tether.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Karma abilities

spike_notes: Bone Skewer and Phantom Undertow available for a coordinated catch
Level 6 with Death From Below available
A low-health target and allied follow-up make an execute route plausible
reasoning: Pyke can create a catch and threaten an execute after allies bring a target low. His stealth and movement help him find an angle, but his passive prevents bonus maximum health from making him a conventional tank; missed control or protected targets can deny the reset route.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Pyke abilities

spike_notes: Shield of Daybreak and Zenith Blade ready with allied follow-up
Eclipse ready before absorbing a committed response
reasoning: Leona can start a close-range control sequence and mark targets for allied damage through Sunlight. She needs a teammate positioned to convert that entry; committing Zenith Blade without follow-up can leave her exposed despite Eclipse's defenses.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Leona abilities

spike_notes: Mana and completed items support repeated spell rotations
Spell Flux and Overload available for a prepared wave or grouped target
Level 6 with Realm Warp available for a coordinated reposition
reasoning: Ryze converts mana and repeated spell access into sustained damage and wave pressure. Flux setup determines whether Overload can spread, while Realm Warp needs a coordinated destination; short reach and interrupted rotations can keep him from delivering the intended fight pattern.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Ryze abilities

spike_notes: Danger Zone Heat is prepared before a trade
Level 6 with The Equalizer available over a contested route
Heat remains below Overheat when another spell is required
reasoning: Rumble can control a narrow approach with The Equalizer and sustained close-range damage. Heat management changes the strength of his basic abilities and can also lock him out of spell casts; opponents who leave the zone or force an early Overheat can break the intended sequence.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Rumble abilities

spike_notes: The Ball is positioned before a contested entry
Command: Protect is ready for the intended ally
reasoning: Orianna can shape an area around the Ball and protect an ally while threatening a coordinated Shockwave. Ball position and allied timing are prerequisites; using protection or moving the Ball changes the available control angle, and an opponent can avoid a grouped entry.
source_name: RiftTheory editorial review of Riot Orianna abilities
